newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico plans debt bailout assets sell-off - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico plans debt bailout assets sell-off - paper.

text.p: Mexico plans to sell off from next April around $13 billion in assets that the government has accumulated from its rescue packages for banks and businesses, Mexico City daily El Financiero said Thursday.

Citing unnamed sources from the Finance Ministry, the newspaper said the assets, 93 percent business credits and seven percent real estate, will be auctioned off to Mexicans and foreigners alike. "The process, whose objective is to recover the support given out to rescue financial institutions, will be open to national and foreign investors through auctions," the newspaper reported.

The government plans to sell off the assets under three programs via an entity called Valuation and Asset Sale. One program is for packets of between 25 and 10,000 of small credits, another is for assets valued between 1.5 million and 50 million pesos and a third is the sale of large corporate assets, the newspaper said.

Since the economic recession of 1995, Mexico has launched a number of rescue plans for banks, mortgage holders, farmers, small businesses and general debtors to ease financial burdens heightened by high interest rates and the economic slump.
